MILESTONE · 100 CONTRIBUTORS · 2026-10-29

100 CONTRIBUTORS.
THE SEARCH ENGINE FOR AI AGENTS.

XERJ ENGINEERING · PUBLISHED 2026-10-29

We published the first XERJ release on July 8, 2026. Today, 113 days later, 100 contributors have committed to XERJ and the repository has 17,478 stars. On the Corpus Hub, 7,226 developers have shared their work. Thank you. You built this with us.

XERJ is a new way for AI to search for data. It is one Rust binary that indexes your code, docs, specs and logs, adds packs from the Corpus Hub, and gives your agent cited answers. Your agent asks, and XERJ finds the passage. Your agent does not have to read whole files.

02 · WHAT YOU GET NOW

A new way for AI to search for data

Agents today mostly find data the slow way. They grep, open a file, read it, and grep again. Each loop costs tokens and time. XERJ gives them a search engine to ask instead.

REFERENCE MEMORY

Memory that works for you, local and remote

SHIPPING

Local. xerj autoindex turns a folder of code, docs, specs and logs into an index on your machine. Your agent can also store facts with POST /_memory/{namespace} and recall them later by meaning or keyword. Each namespace is its own index, so agents do not read each other's memories.

Remote. The Corpus Hub holds pre-indexed packs of public knowledge. Ask a question with xerj ask. XERJ picks the one pack that answers it from a signed catalog, downloads it, and answers on your machine. The Corpus Hub v2 post shows how.

What you get. The default embedder is lexical and runs offline with no API key. Your memory stays on your machine and keeps working when the network does not.

REFERENCE CODING

Search how others solved it, before you write code

SHIPPING

Your coding agent clones and indexes the open-source repositories closest to your task, then searches how they solved the problem. It reads the passage it needs, with its file and line, in place of whole files.

What you get. In our reference coding case study, agents finished the same tasks with 2.7x fewer output tokens at the same 16 of 16 solve rate.

ONE INDEX

Code, docs, logs and data in one place

SHIPPING

Autoindex reads 36 programming languages with symbols and line numbers, plus CSV, JSON, YAML, SQLite, PDF, DOCX, HTML, email and log files. Search is BM25, vector kNN, or both together. XERJ speaks the Elasticsearch API, so the clients you have already connect.

MCP

In the official MCP Registry

SHIPPING

xerj mcp gives your agent 23 tools: search, code search, go to definition, agent memory, and Corpus Hub search and ask. XERJ is listed in the official MCP Registry as io.github.xerj-org/xerj. One command, xerj init, connects it to Claude Code or Cursor. See XERJ for agents.

03 · THANK YOU

This is your project too

To the 100 contributors who sent a fix, a feature, a test or a field report: thank you. To the 7,226 developers who let AI agents learn from their work on the Corpus Hub: thank you. To every agent that ran XERJ in someone's codebase and reported back honestly, good or bad: thank you too.

Your reports told us where XERJ was slow, where it used too much memory, and where it gave a wrong answer. We fixed what you found, and we published the numbers, wins and losses alike, on the benchmarks page.

04 · NEXT

The road to 1.0

The goal for 1.0 is simple: every public claim checked against the release binary, and every input either honoured or refused clearly. These items are on the roadmap for it:

  • An MCP server for the Corpus Hub, so agents can query packs without cloning their sources (#1785).
  • Calibrated confidence on MCP answers, with flags that tell the agent when to hold back or ask a person (#1786).
  • Version-pinned answers with file and line citations (#1789).
  • Symbol and call-graph queries over MCP (#1791).
  • Signed release binaries (#1794).

Before 1.0, we must also fix two open defects. A node can stop when the machine runs out of memory (#1122). Writes do not yet replicate across a multi-node cluster (#1170). Until then, XERJ runs as a single node by default, and we do not claim multi-node production readiness.

Our aim is that every agent can ask a search engine for the data it needs, with a citation, on its own machine. With 100 contributors, we are closer to that than we were in July.

05 · TRY IT

Give your agent a search engine

HAND THIS TO YOUR CODING AGENT Install XERJ (docs: https://xerj.org/llms.txt), index this project's sources, and set up reference coding: clone and index the open-source repos closest to what we're building, and search how they solved a problem before writing code.

Then tell us how it went. A short field report is how you join: what you indexed, what you used it for, and your honest verdict.
